report.source_text: The CBCT revealed a round bony sequestrum at the area of the right upper first molar and almost complete radiopacification of the maxillary sinus (panoramic image of CBCT). The portrayed borders of the sinus floor were discontinuous, revealing a communication between the necrotic bone and the sinus cavity (cross-sectional image of CBCT) (Figure 2). The osteolysis extending beyond the alveolar crest of the maxilla was considered to be associated with the observed chronic sinusitis (almost complete opacification of sinus).

clinician.final_diagnosis: stage 0 medication related osteonecrosis of jaw diagnosis affecting the sinus (classification by American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons [AAOMS])
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 62-year-old female on long-term ibandronate for osteoporosis presented with nonspecific pain, an oral fistula with exudate at a right upper first molar extraction site four months post-extraction. Periapical radiograph showed non-healed alveolar bone and a radiolucent lesion extending to the sinus floor. CBCT confirmed a bony sequestrum at the extraction site, discontinuous sinus floor borders, communication between necrotic bone and maxillary sinus, and near complete sinus opacification interpreted as chronic sinusitis. Clinical exam revealed the oral fistula without bone exposure or odontogenic infection. Microbiological culture ordered but result not documented. Collectively, imaging and clinical findings corroborate stage 0 MRONJ diagnosis with sinus involvement per AAOMS criteria.

Periapical radiograph showed non-healed alveolar bone and radiolucent lesion extending to sinus floor

Patient’s history of 4 years oral ibandronate therapy and recent molar extraction constitute relevant risk factors

Radiological evidence of bony sequestrum and communication with sinus suggest necrosis rather than uncomplicated healing
